requirements.evidence: All the requested pieces exist (app/Models/Entity.php:14-54, app/Models/EntityMembership.php:15-52, app/Models/UserRole.php:5-9, app/Policies/EntityPolicy.php:18-57, app/Policies/EntityMembershipPolicy.php:17-48, factories and both migrations), and the policy rules match the task. However the core DB invariant is not portable: 'ALTER TABLE entity_memberships ADD COLUMN owner_seq ... STORED' (database/migrations/2026_10_29_000001_create_entity_memberships_table.php:22) is rejected by SQLite, which only allows VIRTUAL generated columns in ADD COLUMN, so the migration fails on one of the two required engines. The factory contract is also broken: '#[HasFactory]' with 'use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\HasFactory;' (app/Models/Entity.php:7,13; app/Models/EntityMembership.php:7,14) does not add the HasFactory trait, so Entity::factory()/EntityMembership::factory() do not exist.

conventions.evidence: A hand-rolled, unregistered AuthServiceProvider is added (app/Providers/AuthServiceProvider.php:7-23) instead of relying on Laravel's policy auto-discovery; database/factories/UserFactory.php:18-35 is rewritten by hand; unused imports remain (app/Models/Entity.php:10-11, app/Models/User.php:7, app/Providers/AuthServiceProvider.php:5-6, database/factories/UserFactory.php:7), so the Pint gate in conventions.md would fail; no Pest/PHPUnit tests and no CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] entry. docs/database-schema.md:137,149 is updated, so the docs-in-sync rule is only partly followed.

security.evidence: Authorization rules are implemented correctly: EntityPolicy::manageSettings is owner-only (app/Policies/EntityPolicy.php:53-57), update/delete are owner|admin (:34-43), EntityMembershipPolicy blocks deleting the owner's membership (app/Policies/EntityMembershipPolicy.php:36-42) and allows self-removal (:44-46). Mass assignment is limited via $fillable (app/Models/Entity.php:21, app/Models/EntityMembership.php:17). The gap is that both policies do 'use HandlesAuthorization;' after importing the non-existent Illuminate\Contracts\Auth\HandlesAuthorization (app/Policies/EntityPolicy.php:9,13; app/Policies/EntityMembershipPolicy.php:8,12), so every authorization call fatals instead of returning bool; once fixed, the rules themselves look sound.

tests.evidence: No test files appear anywhere in change.diff. conventions.md requires a test for every feature ('No production code without a test') and tests for the authorization paths; the DB constraint, policies, factories and model relations all ship untested.

simplicity.evidence: Unnecessary pieces and duplication: the AuthServiceProvider is not needed for policy discovery and is never registered (app/Providers/AuthServiceProvider.php); each policy method re-implements the membership lookup with a fresh query (app/Policies/EntityPolicy.php:26-57, app/Policies/EntityMembershipPolicy.php:17-48) even though User::membershipFor() exists (app/Models/User.php:59-62) and is unused; UserFactory drops the cached-password optimisation for a per-row bcrypt() (database/factories/UserFactory.php:35); several unused imports.

readability.evidence: Names and method sizes are good (small single-purpose policy methods, scopes are obvious). But there is a stray blank line between the class declaration and '{' (app/Models/Entity.php:14-16), redundant same-namespace imports (app/Models/Entity.php:9, app/Models/EntityMembership.php:76-78 in the diff), and a misleading comment: 'Owner cannot delete their own membership' (app/Policies/EntityMembershipPolicy.php:38) while the code blocks everyone from deleting the owner's membership; the UserFactory rewrite also deletes useful docblocks.

scope.evidence: database/factories/UserFactory.php:18-35 is an unrelated rewrite that deletes the public unverified() state and remember_token/Str usage, which can break existing tests; app/Providers/AuthServiceProvider.php is an extra file not requested by the task. The rest of the diff (models, enum, migrations, policies, two factories, docs) is on-scope.

issues.explanation: Both policies import Illuminate\Contracts\Auth\HandlesAuthorization (not a real class) and then 'use HandlesAuthorization;', so loading either policy throws 'Trait not found' and every authorization check fatals instead of returning bool.

The owner_seq column is added afterwards with 'ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN ... GENERATED ALWAYS AS (...) STORED'; SQLite forbids STORED generated columns in ADD COLUMN (only VIRTUAL), so the migration fails on SQLite and the required portable one-owner constraint is not delivered — define it with ->storedAs() inside Schema::create instead.
No Pest/PHPUnit tests are added for the migrations, the one-owner DB constraint, the models/relations, the enum, the factories or the policies, violating the project's test-first rule.

'#[HasFactory]' imports Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\HasFactory, which does not exist (the factory trait is Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Factories\HasFactory), so the models never get factory() and the Entity::factory()/EntityMembership::factory() contract is unmet even though the factory classes exist.
The change rewrites UserFactory, deleting the unverified() state (used by existing tests), remember_token and the cached password, which is unrelated to this task and can break the existing suite.

The new provider extends Illuminate\Foundation\Providers\AuthServiceProvider, which does not exist (the base is Illuminate\Foundation\Support\Providers\AuthServiceProvider), and it is never registered in bootstrap/providers.php, so it is dead code; Laravel already auto-discovers EntityPolicy/EntityMembershipPolicy.
Unused imports (Builder, Illuminate\Foundation\Support\Arr, UserRole in User, AuthManager/Gate, Str) and non-sorted/redundant import groups mean the Pint gate required by conventions.md fails.
The slug is just Str::slug($name) with no uniqueness guard, so two distinct company names that slugify identically will violate entities_slug_unique and make factory-created tests flaky.
$membership->entity is dereferenced without a null check, so a membership whose entity was soft-deleted (soft deletes do not cascade) causes a 500 instead of a bool policy result.

Every ability repeats the same 'memberships()->where(user_id)->whereIn(role)->exists()' query although User::membershipFor() (app/Models/User.php:59-62) was just added and could be reused, so membership lookups are duplicated five times.

The docs diff only fixes the ER diagram and two prose lines; it does not document owner_seq/soft deletes in the schema listing, and CHANGELOG.md is not updated under [Unreleased] as conventions.md requires.
There is a blank line between 'class Entity extends Model' and the opening brace, which is inconsistent with the project's Pint-formatted sibling models.
The comment 'Owner cannot delete their own membership' misdescribes the check, which also prevents an owner/admin from deleting the owner's membership.

review.summary: The change adds the Entity/EntityMembership/UserRole models, policies, factories, two migrations and a docs update, and the authorization rules and schema mostly match the task. It cannot merge as is: both policies use a non-existent HandlesAuthorization trait (fatal on load), the owner_seq STORED column is added in a way SQLite rejects, the HasFactory attribute never provides factory(), the UserFactory is destructively rewritten outside scope, and no tests are shipped.
